what: Photo cells inside a card flip one at a time. Dragging horizontally follows the hand (past either end it stretches only by .08), and on release, if dragged over 18% of the cell width or flicked faster than 300px/s it goes to the next or previous image, otherwise it springs back into place (stiffness 480·damping 46·mass .9, settling in about .35s without overshoot). It inherits the release velocity, so a harder flick goes faster. On wide screens, hovering shows 18px round arrows on both sides in .2s, and below 810px a dot pill below replaces the arrows

options.[data-fx-part=track]: Row holding the sections (children) — each child is one section, width matched to the window width
options.[data-fx-part=prev] · [data-fx-part=next: Prev / next buttons (optional, svg arrow inside)
options.[data-fx-part=dots]: Leave empty to fill one dot per section (optional, visible only on narrow screens)
options.cut: Pull distance that counts as a slide (share of cell width), default .18
options.fling: Flick speed (px/s) counted as a flip, default 300
options.elastic: Share that follows when dragged past both ends, default .08
options.--fx-arrow · --fx-arrow-pad: Arrow diameter and edge distance (via style), default 18px·8px
options.fx:slide: Event fired from the element when the section changes (detail.index)

use: …
note: Dragging is this part’s job, so horizontal drags are captured but vertical pushes pass through to the page (touch-action: pan-y). The original uses a motion library’s drag and spring — we followed it by integrating the same spring equation in 1ms steps
